subject.title: fix(ios): use configured speech language for system voice

question: Should the existing `talk.speechLocale` setting intentionally select the installed iOS system voice during provider-failure fallback for upgraded users, instead of leaving system voice choice at Apple’s device default?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and documents the new behavior, but it changes the observable meaning of a persisted, previously recognition-only setting for existing configurations.

options.title: Approve unified speech-locale behavior
options.body: Accept `talk.speechLocale` as the shared iOS recognition and native-fallback voice locale, then merge after required checks complete.

options.title: Keep recognition-only semantics
options.body: Reject the behavior expansion and require a separately designed, explicitly named voice-selection setting or product path before changing fallback speech.

recommendation.title: Approve unified speech-locale behavior
recommendation.body: Accept `talk.speechLocale` as the shared iOS recognition and native-fallback voice locale, then merge after required checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review identified both the native fallback invariant and the cross-surface configuration contract that frame the remaining product decision.
